title: The right-boundary transition
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,B,R\in\mathbb{N}$, and fix a schedule-alphabet input, a base configuration, an input-head position, an integer budget-head position, and a budget tape. Starting in right-edge phase with unary head at $B+1$ on the unary tape with $B$ markers and guide head at $R+1$ on the partial guide with $R+1$ copied cells, one step enters layout-return phase $0$, moves the unary and guide heads left to $B$ and $R$, respectively, and changes the guide tape to the right guide of radius $R$; the other configuration data is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
a schedule-alphabet input, base configuration, and input-head position
integer budget-head position and budget tape
unary head is at $B+1$ on the unary tape with $B$ markers
guide head is at $R+1$ on the partial guide with $R+1$ copied cells
replaced:
From a setup configuration in the right-edge phase with unary head at cell $B+1$ over
the unary tape with $B$ markers and guide head at cell $R+1$ over the partial guide
with $R+1$ copied cells, one step writes the right outer boundary marker at guide cell
$R+1$, moves the unary and guide heads one cell left (to $B$ and $R$), and enters the
first layout-return phase; the resulting guide tape is the right guide of radius $R$.
